subject: prd/argus-ledger-lint
statement: The cross-document arm shall treat a `delivery:` reference as an in-scope **citation** — a candidate for FR-3/FR-4/UB-2 classification — only when it is a resolvable citation into an existing ledger: a `delivery:<concrete-slug>#<anchor>` reference whose `<concrete-slug>` names an existing `docs/problems/<concrete-slug>/delivery.md` ledger. A `delivery:` string that names no existing ledger directory — in particular a grammar/prose illustration written with the literal metavariable placeholder `<slug>` (angle-bracketed), which resolves to no `docs/problems/<slug>/` directory — is **not** a citation and shall be left untouched (no defect, no classification). The scan's corpus is every tracked document in the repo; the boundary is the target's resolvability, never the string's textual shape alone.
rationale: citation-target legality for the ledger classes is the new behavior this PRD introduces (absent from docgate-v1/v2; `doc-link-integrity` owns relative-link resolution only — T-2); the arm's own governing corpus (this PRD, the frozen record, argus-artifacts §3.2/§3.4) is saturated with literal-`<slug>` prose illustrations, so an unbounded scan would false-red its own basis, breaking the §3.3 guardrail and NR-1
fit_criterion: on a fixture pairing a real `delivery:<concrete-slug>#E-n` citation into a seeded ledger with prose that merely quotes `delivery:<slug>#E-n` (literal `<slug>`) and a `delivery:no-such-slug#E-1` mention of a non-existent ledger, the arm classifies only the resolvable citation and reports zero defects on the two non-citations; and on the repo's own citation-bearing prose (this PRD, the record, the design) the arm is green
